messages:
Taylor: New user report: React quickstart printed "200 OK" then the UI never showed streaming tokens. They assumed success and closed the app.
Rhea: Did they try curl to compare?
Taylor: Yep — curl against the same key returned chunked events. The quickstart logs only had "response complete: 200" and no data callbacks.
Marcus (devex): Any billing state on the workspace? This pattern smells like billing gating.
Taylor: Console shows "trial pending" and a small banner about activating trial. User says they ignored it because quickstart seemed successful.
BillingBot: Reminder: streaming endpoints require active billing for full chunked delivery. For billing_inactive workspaces the gateway may return a short non-chunked response to limit resources. See /docs/billing for guidance.
June (sdk): This is rough DX: many SDKs treat an immediate 200+EOF as success. We should either ensure the server never returns an ambiguous 200 for programmatic clients or make SDKs detect the pattern and surface a clear billing error.
Rhea: Which is less breaking? Change server to 402 or change SDK heuristics?
Marcus (devex): Prefer server-side clarity: return 402 + JSON {code:billing_inactive} for API/stream gating or include an initial error chunk for streams. SDKs should also stop auto-retrying on 401/403 when billing metadata is present.
June (sdk): Agreed. Short-term SDK mitigation: if request was a stream and headers lack Transfer-Encoding: chunked and body length < 1KB and body contains "billing" or "activate", throw BillingInactiveError with a console link. That'll make quickstarts fail loudly. I'll open a patch for JS/React SDKs.
Taylor: Also add a quickstart preflight in the template: call GET /v1/workspace and show a modal if billing != active. Simple UX fix prevents confusion.
Marcus (devex): Docs update too: add a troubleshooting section called "200 but no streaming events" with repro and steps. Emil?
Emil (docs): On it. I'll add the snippet and the recommended workarounds: activate trial / add payment method / create new key after activation.
BillingBot: Note: orgs created via SSO that skip billing activation are the most affected cohort. Telemetry suggested a small but measurable drop-off in the first 24 hours for these orgs.
Marcus (devex): Action items: 1) infra: return explicit billing error for programmatic clients (402/structured json) and ensure streams include an initial error chunk when gating (marcus -> infra), 2) sdk: detect non-chunked short responses for streams and throw BillingInactiveError (june -> sdk), 3) quickstarts: add billing preflight check and explicit onboarding copy (taylor -> devex-dx), 4) docs: add troubleshooting note (emil -> docs), 5) telemetry: add first_call_stream_billing_mismatch metric (infra -> telemetry).
June (sdk): I'll aim for a small SDK release with the heuristic this week. Marcus, can infra add an X-Redwood-Error header for a quick signal? SDKs can check that too.
Marcus (devex): Yes, infra can add X-Redwood-Error=billing_inactive in the short term. We'll prioritize structured 402 behavior in the next deploy.
Taylor: I'll reply to the customer with the workaround (activate trial or add payment method) and tell them we're shipping an SDK quick-fix.
Emil (docs): Drafting the docs now; will link here when ready.
Marcus (devex): Once SDK patch and infra header land, post a short note in #announcements so community knows quickstarts may need an update.
Taylor: Thanks all — will update this thread as items land. :thumbsup:
